title: Lesson 19: لَنْ — Negating the Future with Emphasis, and the Family of حُرُوف النَّاصِبَة
summary: The lesson's new item is لَنْ, which negates a مُضَارِع verb specifically in the future and does so emphatically — لَا أَذْهَبُ could mean I am not going now or later, but لَنْ أَذْهَبَ can only mean I will not go. It also joins أَنْ and the لَام in the family of حُرُوف النَّاصِبَة, so it puts the verb into the accusative and drops the نُون in the same way. The session gathers half a dozen Qur'ānic instances and sorts out عِنْدَمَا, إِذَا and لَمَّا along the way.
key_points: لَنْ negates a مُضَارِع verb for the future, and carries emphasis: لَا أَذْهَبُ إِلَى السُّوقِ is ambiguous between now and later, while لَنْ أَذْهَبَ settles it as I will not go.
The particles of negation now in hand: مَا for the مَاضِي, لَا for the مُضَارِع (present or future, leaving the verb's ending alone), and لَنْ for the future alone, which changes the ending.

لَنْ belongs to the حُرُوف النَّاصِبَة along with أَنْ and the لَام of purpose — and كَيْ, which comes later. All of them put the مُضَارِع into the accusative and all drop the نُون from forms that carry one: تَنَالُونَ becomes لَنْ تَنَالُوا, تَسْتَطِيعُونَ becomes لَنْ تَسْتَطِيعُوا.
Verbs ending in a long alif, such as تَرَى, do not change whatever precedes them — hence لَنْ تَرَانِي.
نُون النِّسْوَة is unaffected by لَنْ just as by أَنْ.

عِنْدَمَا (when) is عِنْدَ plus مَا joined together. Among the words for when, لَمَّا is used only of the past, إِذَا points to the future, and عِنْدَمَا is flexible across past, present and future. These belong to conditional sentences.
The second person is built into the verb itself, so تَشْتَرِي already means you buy — no separate pronoun is needed.
بَقِيَ، يَبْقَى means to remain in the sense of what is left over, the same as Urdu bāqī; لَبِثَ is to stay somewhere for a time before moving on.
آسِف means sorry, and the root also carries sorrow or regret — يَا أَسَفَى عَلَىٰ يُوسُفَ, and Mūsā عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام returning غَضْبَانَ أَسِفًا, angry and grieved.
أَوَّلًا means firstly, in a sequence of time, and carries a fatḥa because it functions as a ظَرْف.
هُنُود is the plural of هِنْدِيّ, meaning people from India, and should not be confused with هِنْدُوس, Hindus.

The rules of tajwīd apply to reciting the Qur'ān, not to reading ordinary Arabic — so لَنْ يَذْهَبَ is read plainly, without the idghām the Qur'ān's recitation would require, because the Qur'ān has its own method of recitation taught by the Prophet ﷺ and passed down.

Vocabulary: سِفَارَة (embassy) with سَفِير (ambassador), اِعْتَمَرَ، يَعْتَمِرُ (to perform ʿumrah), مَصْرِف with its plural مَصَارِف (banks), قَرِيبًا (soon), عِلَاج (treatment), مَوْجُود (present or available), and أَلَا as simply هَمْزَة الِاسْتِفْهَام with لَا.
The teacher's study advice: keep a running vocabulary list and revisit it, though the real remedy is continuous reading — words you meet daily need no revision, just as English vocabulary needs none.
questions: [00:01:02] Q: What is the difference between إِذَا, عِنْدَمَا and لَمَّا, which all mean when? — A: لَمَّا is for the past only, إِذَا points to the future, and عِنْدَمَا is flexible and works for any tense.
[00:02:01] Q: Where is the you in that sentence? — A: Built into the verb: يَشْتَرِي is he buys, تَشْتَرِي is you buy, so the تَـ carries it.
[00:03:00] Q: Is it mā wajadtuhu meaning you will not find it? — A: No, مَا negates the past, and وَجَدْتُهُ is past tense, so it means I did not find it.
[00:07:00] Q: Was لَنْ used where the people said they would be overtaken? — A: No. There they said something else, and Mūsā عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام answered إِنَّ مَعِيَ رَبِّي سَيَهْدِينِ.
[00:14:07] Q: Can آسِف mean sorrow or grief? — A: Yes — the same root as Yaʿqūb عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام's يَا أَسَفَى عَلَىٰ يُوسُفَ, and in أَنَا آسِف it is how you say I am sorry.

[00:15:00] Q: Was the one who brought the throne an angel? — A: No. The jinn was the first who offered; the second, described as الَّذِي عِنْدَهُ عِلْمٌ مِّنَ الْكِتَابِ, is said to have been a pious human being.

[00:15:00] Q: Could someone have that kind of power today, and would it be black magic? — A: These are كَرَامَات, gifts Allah عَزَّ وَجَلَّ grants to some people. They are possible but rare, many claimants are frauds, and those truly given such a gift should not display it.
[00:19:05] Q: Why is it combined into one sound in the Qur'ān but not here? — A: Because the Qur'ān has its own rules of recitation; ordinary Arabic reading does not apply idghām.
[00:23:00] Q: How does بَقِيَ differ from لَبِثَ? — A: بَقِيَ is what remains or is left behind, as in Urdu bāqī; لَبِثَ is staying somewhere for a period before moving on.

options: A مُضَارِع verb, specifically in the future
quiz.a: It is confined to the future, and adds emphasis — I will not.

quiz.q: What does لَنْ do to the verb's ending?
options: Puts it into the accusative, or drops its نُون
quiz.a: It is one of the حُرُوف النَّاصِبَة, so it behaves exactly like أَنْ and the لَام.

quiz.q: How does لَنْ differ from لَا in meaning?
options: لَا can mean now or later; لَنْ fixes the meaning as the future, with emphasis
لَا is only for the past
quiz.a: لَا أَذْهَبُ is ambiguous; لَنْ أَذْهَبَ is unmistakably about the future.

quiz.q: Which three particles of negation has the class now covered?
quiz.a: مَا for the past, لَا for the present or future, and لَنْ for the future alone.

quiz.q: What becomes of تَنَالُونَ after لَنْ?
quiz.a: لَن تَنَالُوا الْبِرَّ — the نُون drops, exactly as it does after أَنْ.

quiz.q: Why does تَرَى not change in لَنْ تَرَانِي?
options: Because verbs ending in a long alif do not change
Because لَنْ never affects the first person
quiz.a: The teacher singled this verb out: whatever precedes it, it stays تَرَى.

quiz.q: What two words make up عِنْدَمَا?
quiz.a: عِنْدَ plus مَا, joined to mean when.

quiz.q: Which of the words for when is restricted to the past?
quiz.a: لَمَّا is used of the past, إِذَا of the future, and عِنْدَمَا is flexible.
سِفَارَة is the embassy; سَفِير is the ambassador.
The plural of هِنْدِيّ. The teacher warned against confusing it with هِنْدُوس, which means Hindus.

quran_examples.arabic: لَن تَنَالُوا الْبِرَّ حَتَّىٰ تُنفِقُوا مِمَّا تُحِبُّونَ
quran_examples.transliteration: lan tanālū al-birra ḥattā tunfiqū mimmā tuḥibbūn
quran_examples.translation: You will never attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love.
quran_examples.note: The first example offered, noted as the opening of the fourth juz'. تَنَالُونَ loses its نُون after لَنْ, and مِمَّا is مِنْ with مَا الْمَوْصُولَة.

quran_examples.arabic: وَلَن تَسْتَطِيعُوا أَن تَعْدِلُوا بَيْنَ النِّسَاءِ وَلَوْ حَرَصْتُمْ ۖ فَلَا تَمِيلُوا كُلَّ الْمَيْلِ
quran_examples.transliteration: wa-lan tastaṭīʿū an taʿdilū bayna al-nisāʾi wa-law ḥaraṣtum, fa-lā tamīlū kulla al-mayl
quran_examples.translation: And you will never be able to be equal between wives, even if you should strive to do so. So do not incline completely.
quran_examples.note: Both لَنْ and أَنْ in one āyah, each dropping a نُون. The teacher explained its sense: equal love is not within human control, but showing favour by gifts, attention or time is, and that is what is forbidden.

quran_examples.arabic: قَالَ لَن تَرَانِي وَلَٰكِنِ انظُرْ إِلَى الْجَبَلِ
quran_examples.transliteration: qāla lan tarānī wa-lākini nẓur ilā al-jabal
quran_examples.translation: He said: You will not see Me, but look at the mountain.
quran_examples.note: A student's answer. The teacher explained it concerns this world — humans lack the capacity now, and Allah عَزَّ وَجَلَّ will create it in the Hereafter. It also contains the command اُنْظُرْ.

quran_examples.translation: Does man think that We will not assemble his bones?
quran_examples.note: Offered in class: نَجْمَعُ takes the fatḥa after لَنْ, and the teacher drew out the meaning — his bones scattered in the ground, and the question whether they will be gathered and he resurrected.

quran_examples.arabic: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَن تُغْنِيَ عَنْهُمْ أَمْوَالُهُمْ وَلَا أَوْلَادُهُم مِّنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئًا
quran_examples.transliteration: inna alladhīna kafarū lan tughniya ʿanhum amwāluhum wa-lā awlāduhum mina llāhi shayʾā
quran_examples.translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve — never will their wealth or their children avail them against Allah at all.
quran_examples.note: Another instance raised in class: تُغْنِي becomes تُغْنِيَ with the fatḥa after لَنْ.

quran_examples.arabic: قَالَ لَا ۖ إِنَّ مَعِيَ رَبِّي سَيَهْدِينِ
quran_examples.transliteration: qāla lā, inna maʿiya rabbī sa-yahdīn
quran_examples.translation: He said: No. Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me.
quran_examples.note: Mūsā عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام's reply when his people feared being overtaken — cited as the place where لَنْ is not used, with سَيَهْدِينِ carrying the future سَـ instead.

quran_examples.translation: And he said: Oh, my sorrow over Yūsuf.
quran_examples.note: Cited for the root behind آسِف, showing it carries grief and regret as well as apology.

quran_examples.arabic: قَالَ الَّذِي عِندَهُ عِلْمٌ مِّنَ الْكِتَابِ أَنَا آتِيكَ بِهِ قَبْلَ أَن يَرْتَدَّ إِلَيْكَ طَرْفُكَ
quran_examples.transliteration: qāla alladhī ʿindahu ʿilmun mina al-kitābi anā ātīka bihi qabla an yartadda ilayka ṭarfuk
quran_examples.translation: Said one who had knowledge from the Scripture: I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you.
quran_examples.note: The āyah behind the discussion of كَرَامَات and the name Āṣif. It also carries قَبْلَ أَنْ with the verb in the accusative, the construction of the previous lessons.
